candidates.name: HM Land Registry plans: the basis of HM Land Registry plans (PG40s1)
verified_facts: Official HM Land Registry guidance explains the origins and scales of Ordnance Survey mapping and how that mapping relates to HM Land Registry plans.
The guide remains the basis reference for interpreting the mapping framework beneath title plans.
semantic_limits: An Ordnance Survey base-map scale does not make a title-plan boundary an exact legal boundary.
Mapping scale/planimetric accuracy must not be converted into vertical terrain uncertainty.

candidates.name: Preparing plans for HM Land Registry applications (PG40s2)
verified_facts: Official guidance is dedicated to preparing plans for HM Land Registry applications.
The publication was last updated 13 October 2025 and applies to England and Wales.
semantic_limits: Application-plan quality requirements are legal/planimetric evidence controls, not elevation measurement accuracy.

candidates.name: Guidance for preparing plans for HM Land Registry applications
verified_facts: The detailed guidance covers why good-quality plans matter and gives preparation rules for first registrations and transfers/leases of part.
It also covers unusual extents, verbal descriptions and electronic lodgement of plans.
semantic_limits: A compliant application plan still does not establish the vertical terrain range of a parcel.

candidates.name: Plan requirements and surveying specification (PG41s5)
verified_facts: Official HM Land Registry guidance provides technical plan and surveying specification information for plans lodged with the registry.
The guide is aimed at developers, legal advisers and surveyors.
semantic_limits: Registry surveying specifications govern plan evidence and must not be substituted for LiDAR/DTM vertical-error specifications.

candidates.name: HM Land Registry plans: practice guides collection
verified_facts: The official collection lists the current HM Land Registry plan guides together in one place.
As of verification, PG40 supplement 3 and supplement 4 show 1 June 2026 updates and supplement 5 shows a 13 July 2026 update.
semantic_limits: A collection/version page is freshness and routing evidence; it does not itself prove parcel geometry or terrain values.

candidates.name: Boundary agreements and determined boundaries — detailed PG40s4
verified_facts: The guidance states a determined boundary records the exact line rather than the ordinary general boundary.
For measurement-based determined-boundary plans, measurements are required to be horizontal, taken from defined permanent features and accurate to ±10 mm.
The plan must identify start, end and turning points and show enough surrounding detail to locate the general position on Ordnance Survey mapping.
semantic_limits: The ±10 mm requirement is a horizontal boundary-plan measurement requirement, not LiDAR vertical RMSE.
Determined-boundary evidence is exceptional and must be explicitly present before exact-boundary claims are made.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 Documentation
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 is a detailed DTM of Great Britain supplied as five-metre grid points and five-metre contours.
The product is updated quarterly in January, April, July and October.
The grid and contour forms are created from the same source data and supplied in 5 km by 5 km tiles.
semantic_limits: OS Terrain 5 remains a secondary terrain cross-check for this slot and does not replace Environment Agency 1 m DTM evidence.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 Technical Specification
verified_facts: The technical specification distinguishes OS Terrain 5 from the lower-resolution Terrain 50 product.
Terrain 5 grid uses regular 5 m post spacing while contours use 5 m intervals.
Terrain GML expresses its coordinate reference system using EPSG:27700 British National Grid.
semantic_limits: A product format/CRS declaration does not prove parcel-specific acquisition time or survey lineage.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 Overview
verified_facts: The overview describes regular 5 m grid spacing and 5 m contour intervals.
It says the product is maintained through an integrated 3-to-5-year flying programme and is synchronised with other product updates.
It provides full Great Britain coverage and is designed to work with Ordnance Survey large-scale data.
semantic_limits: Maintenance-cycle information is product currency evidence, not parcel acquisition time or EA survey identity.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 data structure
verified_facts: OS states grid height values are calculated at the centre of the pixel.
Mean high and low water breaklines use tile-average height values derived from local tide tables.
The documentation warns that small discrete steps in tidal-water height can occur between adjacent tiles.
semantic_limits: Pixel-centre and tidal-tile conventions are processing/model semantics and not guarantees of point-observation accuracy.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 source data
verified_facts: The source DTM is captured as a triangulated irregular network using mass points, breaklines and photogrammetric or automated methods.
Grid and contour products are interpolated from the source TIN.
The source records bare-earth surface and removes buildings, supported structures and vegetation.
OS distinguishes source positional-accuracy requirements from stated product accuracy and evaluates absolute accuracy using RMSE against real-world points.
semantic_limits: OS source-TIN accuracy criteria are not Environment Agency LiDAR survey RMSE and must stay a secondary cross-check.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 metadata
verified_facts: Terrain 5 provides GEMINI-style XML metadata on a per-tile basis.
Metadata includes tile reference, spatial representation, coordinate reference systems, version number and lineage/reason-for-change information.
Lineage text can distinguish newly created imagery, partial revision and imagery checked with no change.
semantic_limits: OS tile lineage describes Terrain 5 maintenance and cannot establish the EA composite contributing survey for a parcel.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 product supply
verified_facts: Terrain 5 is supplied as 5 km by 5 km tiles with full Great Britain coverage.
The national grid supply contains 10,579 data tiles and per-tile metadata files.
OS states full-tile resupplies are issued quarterly in January, April, July and October.
semantic_limits: Tile supply cadence is distribution/update evidence, not a parcel observation timestamp.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 grid data
verified_facts: Terrain 5 grid data are supplied as ASCII with GML support.
The GML carries metadata such as location, grid spacing and vertical reference system while spatial height values are held in the external ASCII grid block.
The ASCII grid can be consumed directly by common GIS software.
semantic_limits: A metadata wrapper or file encoding must not be mistaken for independent numeric terrain evidence.

candidates.name: OGC API - Maps - Part 1: Core
verified_facts: The standard specifies discovery and retrieval of maps through Web APIs.
It is oriented to map distribution and does not require exposing the underlying native data store.
semantic_limits: Rendered maps are portrayal evidence and must not be promoted to numeric DTM cell observations.

candidates.name: OGC API - Tiles - Part 1: Core
verified_facts: The standard defines discovery and retrieval of tiled geospatial resources using tile matrix sets.
Coverage tiles can contain gridded observations or measurements and may be generated with subsetting and resampling.
Tile encoding can use formats such as GeoTIFF or netCDF.
semantic_limits: A tiled or resampled coverage response is derived delivery evidence unless native sampling semantics are independently established.
